1_Learning_Objective.Title: 🎯 The "Why Are We Learning This?" (Learning Objective)
1_Learning_Objective.Content: This chapter helps your child understand why we need food, the names of our three main meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner), and the difference between healthy 'grow' food and sometimes-only 'junk' food.

2_The_Hook.Title: 🪝 The Hook (How to start the conversation)
2_The_Hook.Content: Hold up a toy car or point to a vehicle outside. Ask: **'What happens to a car if we don't put petrol in it?'** (It stops!). Say: **'Exactly! Our bodies are like amazing cars, but our petrol is FOOD! Let's learn about the best fuel for our bodies.'**

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'We put fuel in our bodies three times a day. In the morning, we eat Breakfast. In the middle of the day, we eat Lunch. At night, before bed, we eat Dinner.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Draw a quick picture of a Sun rising, a Sun high in the sky, and a Moon. Have them place a spoon on the 'Breakfast' sun, the 'Lunch' sun, and the 'Dinner' moon.

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Fruits, veggies, and milk make us grow tall and strong! Chips and sweets are yummy, but they are just for fun sometimes, not for growing.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Open the fridge together. Take out an apple and a chocolate/biscuit. Ask them, 'Which one makes our muscles strong?' Flex your arms together!

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Before our hands touch our food, they must be squeaky clean! We must wash our hands so tiny germs don't get a free ride into our tummies.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Put a little flour or powder on their hands and call them 'germs'. Ask them to try wiping it off without water (it's hard!), then use soap and water to show how they disappear.

4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Title: 🚧 Common Stumbling Blocks (What to watch out for)
4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Content:
Kids sometimes mix up **Lunch** and **Dinner**. 
*   **How to clarify:** Associate them with locations. 'Lunch is what we eat when you are at school or in the afternoon. Dinner is what we eat when everyone is home and it's dark outside.'

Questions.Question: What is the meal we eat in the morning called?
Is ice cream a 'grow strong' food or a 'sometimes' fun food?
Why do we wash our hands before eating our Lunch?
Questions.Expected_Answer: To wash away germs so we don't get sick.

Activities.Name: 1. The 'Happy Tooth, Sad Tooth' Sorting Game
Activities.Description: Draw a smiling tooth and a crying tooth on two sheets of paper. Give your child grocery store flyers or real food items, and have them sort the healthy food to the happy tooth and sweets to the sad tooth.

Activities.Name: 2. Pretend Restaurant
Activities.Description: Give them a notepad. Pretend you are at a restaurant and say, 'I would like to order a healthy Breakfast please!' Let them pretend to cook and serve you eggs or fruit.

Activities.Name: 3. The Hand Washing Song
Activities.Description: Make up a 20-second handwashing song to sing at the sink before dinner. E.g., 'Wash, wash, wash your hands, make them nice and clean!'

Activities.Name: 4. Grocery Bag Guessing
Activities.Description: Put 3 different fruits or vegetables in an opaque bag. Have your child reach in, feel the shape, and guess what healthy food it is before pulling it out.
